owensboro-ky.heading: Auto insurance in Owensboro
paragraphs_html: Owensboro workers average a 17.1-minute commute, according to the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 American Community Survey, so most driving here is short trips across town and around Daviess County. Insurers rate a car by where it is kept and how it is used, so give us the real commute and any business driving when we quote.

A Kentucky auto policy has to carry at least $25,000 of bodily injury liability per person and $50,000 per accident, plus $25,000 for property damage, or a $60,000 single limit, along with basic reparation benefits (KRS 304.39-110(1)). We quote higher limits next to the minimum so you can compare the cost. Start with our auto insurance page.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Owensboro city, Kentucky (mean travel time to work, 2020-2024)

owensboro-ky.heading: Home and renters insurance in Owensboro
paragraphs_html: The National Weather Service puts flood stage for the Ohio River at Owensboro at 40 feet, moderate flooding at 44 feet and major flooding at 49 feet. FEMA notes that most homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage, so a home near the river or a low-lying creek needs a separate flood insurance policy, bought well before the water rises.

In Owensboro, 57.4 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied (2020-2024 American Community Survey), so a large share of residents rent. A landlord's policy covers the building, not a tenant's belongings or liability, which is what renters insurance is for. Owners can start with home insurance.

owensboro-ky.heading: Business insurance in Owensboro and Daviess County
paragraphs_html: The Census Bureau counts 2,385 employer establishments in Daviess County (2023) and 6,798 nonemployer businesses, the self-employed and other firms with no payroll (2024). A common starting point for both is general liability and commercial property, often packaged together in a business owner's policy, with commercial auto for vehicles the business owns.
A lease, a customer contract or a vendor agreement usually states the coverage and limits it expects. Send us that page before you sign, and we will check the policy against it.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Daviess County, Kentucky (employer establishments, 2023; nonemployer establishments, 2024)

owensboro-ky.heading: Workers' compensation for Daviess County employers
paragraphs_html: Daviess County employer establishments had 43,758 employees in 2023, by the Census Bureau's count. In Kentucky, a business with one or more employees is subject to the workers' compensation law unless it is engaged solely in agriculture (KRS 342.630), and it must insure that liability or qualify to pay compensation directly (KRS 342.340).
Owners, and qualified partners or LLC members, are covered only if they elect coverage by an endorsement to the policy (KRS 342.012). Our workers' compensation page starts a quote.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Daviess County, Kentucky (total employment, 2023)

owensboro-ky.heading: Life insurance for Owensboro families
paragraphs_html: Owensboro has 25,451 households, averaging 2.30 people each (2020-2024 American Community Survey). Life insurance pays the people who depend on your income if you die, so the amount usually starts from that income and from debts such as a mortgage.

Term life covers a set number of years, for example while children are at home or a loan is outstanding. Whole life lasts for life and builds cash value, at a higher premium for the same amount. Ask us to compare term lengths and amounts with you.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Owensboro city, Kentucky (households and persons per household, 2020-2024)

mt-washington-ky.heading: Auto insurance for Mt Washington commuters
paragraphs_html: Mt Washington workers average a 29.2-minute trip to work (2020-2024 American Community Survey), so daily mileage adds up. The distance you drive is one of the things insurers weigh, so give us the actual figure when we quote.

Kentucky's floor is $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident for bodily injury plus $25,000 for property damage, or one $60,000 single limit, and every policy includes basic reparation benefits (KRS 304.39-110(1)). Insurers must also make underinsured motorist coverage available on request (KRS 304.39-320(2)). See auto insurance.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Mount Washington city, Kentucky (mean travel time to work, 2020-2024)

mt-washington-ky.heading: Home insurance in a fast-growing city
paragraphs_html: Mt Washington grew from 9,117 residents in the 2010 Census to 18,090 in the 2020 Census, and 86.1 percent of its occupied homes are owner-occupied (2020-2024 American Community Survey). New and older homes are rated differently: roof age, wiring, plumbing and the cost to rebuild all count, so set the dwelling limit from current construction costs rather than the purchase price.

FEMA notes that most homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage. Look up your address on FEMA's Flood Map Service Center before you buy, and ask us about flood insurance alongside your home insurance.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Mount Washington city, Kentucky (Census 2010 and 2020 population; owner-occupied housing unit rate, 2020-2024)

mt-washington-ky.heading: Life insurance for Mt Washington households
paragraphs_html: Mt Washington's 6,936 households average 2.65 people, and the median household income is $96,239 (2020-2024 American Community Survey). When a household relies on one or two paychecks, the question is how long that income would need replacing and what debts would need paying off.
Term life fits a need with an end date, such as a mortgage. Whole life stays in force for life. Disability insurance protects the paycheck itself if an illness or injury keeps you from working.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Mount Washington city, Kentucky (households, persons per household, median household income, 2020-2024)

mt-washington-ky.heading: Insurance for Bullitt County contractors
paragraphs_html: Census QuickFacts lists 654 building permits for Bullitt County in 2025. Before a local building official issues a permit, the builder must show proof of workers' compensation coverage, or certify an exemption in writing on the commissioner's form (KRS 342.610(6)). A contractor is also liable for an uninsured subcontractor's injured employees (KRS 342.610(2)), which is why subs are asked for certificates before they start.

For the job itself, builders risk covers a structure while it is going up and general liability answers injury and damage claims. Our general contractors page lists Kentucky's subcontractor and bond rules.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Bullitt County, Kentucky (building permits, 2025)
